#### What this PR does / why we need it:
Marks v2beta2 HPA status conditions field as optional. `conditions` is a subfield of `status` which is already optional. This was found when serializing a valid HPA with no status field - this resulted in an unnecessary client-side apply ValidationError, stating that it was missing the required field `conditions`. This error should be fixed since it is a subfield of `status` which is not required.

issue_context.title: NewSerializerWithOptions yaml for v2beta2 HPA cannot be applied with ValidationError
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


#### What happened:

Serializing a v2beta2 HorizontalPodAutoscaler with `NewSerializerWithOptions` (and `NewYAMLSerializer`) produces yaml that cannot be applied due to a ValidationError on the `conditions` field which is under the _optional_ field `status`.

#### What you expected to happen:

A valid HPA serialized with `NewSerializerWithOptions` should be able to be applied to the cluster with no validation errors, without filling out the optional `status` field.

Other valid objects (such as Namespaces and Deployments) can be applied directly, without filling out their optional `status` fields.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

Run this to generate the serialized yaml (same outcome with both `NewSerializerWithOptions` and `NewYAMLSerializer` functions)
```
package main

import (
  "os"

  autoscalingv2beta2 "k8s.io/api/autoscaling/v2beta2"
  metav1 "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1"
  "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/runtime/serializer/json"
  "k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes/scheme"
)

func main() {
  hpa := autoscalingv2beta2.HorizontalPodAutoscaler{
    TypeMeta: metav1.TypeMeta{
      Kind: "HorizontalPodAutoscaler",
      APIVersion: "autoscaling/v2beta2",
    },
    ObjectMeta: metav1.ObjectMeta{
      Name: "hpatest",
      Namespace: "test",
    },
  }

  //encoder := json.NewYAMLSerializer(json.DefaultMetaFactory, scheme.Scheme, scheme.Scheme)
  encoder := json.NewSerializerWithOptions(json.DefaultMetaFactory, scheme.Scheme, scheme.Scheme, json.SerializerOptions{Yaml: true,})
  encoder.Encode(&hpa, os.Stdout)
}
```

Running the go code should yield this yaml:
```
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2beta2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: null
  name: hpatest
  namespace: test
spec:
  maxReplicas: 0
  scaleTargetRef:
    kind: ""
    name: ""
status:
  conditions: null
  currentMetrics: null
  currentReplicas: 0
  desiredReplicas: 0
```

Writing the above yaml to a file hpa.yaml and applying it (with `kubectl apply -f hpa.yaml`) will result in:

```
error: error validating "hpa.yaml": error validating data: ValidationError(HorizontalPodAutoscaler.status): missing required field "conditions" in io.k8s.api.autoscaling.v2beta2.HorizontalPodAutoscalerStatus; if you choose to ignore these errors, turn validation off with --validate=false
```

#### Anything else we need to know?:

#### Environment:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): Server: v1.20.2, Client: v1.20.4
- go version: go1.16 darwin/amd64
- go.mod has:
```
require (
  k8s.io/api v0.17.0
  k8s.io/apimachinery v0.17.0
  k8s.io/client-go v0.17.0
)
```
cc @ashleykasim 
cc @paulnivin
comments: marking conditions as +optional in the API type would resolve the client-side apply error

It would remove the validation error, but I'd be concerned about any side effects or unwanted outcomes when moving that field from required to optional. A somewhat analogous field [DeploymentStatus.Conditions](https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/api/apps/v1#DeploymentStatus) is required. But if you anticipate this won't change much else, that will work.

> if you choose to ignore these errors, turn validation off with --validate=false

Client-side validation is non-authoritative, and problematic for the reasons described in this issue ... the client is disallowing a request the server would actually have no problems with. No field the server would permit to be empty (e.g. succeeds with `--validate=false`) should be marked as required for this reason.

> A somewhat analogous field DeploymentStatus.Conditions is required.

fwiw, openapi schema generation marks fields tagged as `omitempty` as optional:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-openapi/blob/master/pkg/generators/openapi.go#L80-L88

review_comments:
Other optional slices are annotated with `json:omitempty` and `protobuf:opt`.  This one should be too.

We should also ask for API review of this change, in particular for backward compatability.  E.g. what happens when you use serialize an HPA with `nil` conditions?  Before it would produce an empty slice.  Afterward it would produce a `null`.  Does that mean a new version of kubectl might send an invalid protobuf to a previous server version?  I don't think you can safely make a protobuf field optional after the fact.

I'm fine with adding `json:omitempty`, but I don't think it should be annotated with `protobuf:opt` here. The current annotation `protobuf:rep` will allow this field to be repeated any number of times including zero, while `protobuf:opt` will allow zero or one of this field but not more, which sounds more like a breaking change. (Referencing https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/proto#specifying_field_rules)

In addition, other optional slices here (HorizontalPodAutoscalerSpec.Metrics, HPAScalingRules.Policies) have `json:omitempty` but not `protobuf:opt`. (Note that the above HorizontalPodAutoscalerStatus.CurrentMetrics actually has neither tag, but that isn't the concern here.)

You are totally right about the `protobuf:rep` tag.  I overlooked that.

I think all the slices should have `json:omitempty`.  Policies does, just CurrentMetrics is missing.  Will you please add it?  Otherwise this is good-to-go.
Yep! Wanted to make sure we didn't need any other changes. Added the `json:omitempty` tag.
